_notes: Nations are anonymised as 'Nation A' and 'Nation B' to limit historical-outcome leakage: a named dyad lets a model retrieve how the real episode ended instead of reasoning about the situation.

The event is deliberately ambiguous. Its observable signature is consistent with BOTH a survivability hedge and launch preparation. Ambiguity is what forces the theorist panel to matter; an unambiguous event would be decided by the intelligence brief alone.

ground_truth_detail is HOST-ONLY. It exists so that misperception can be scored by the analyst, not so that an agent can be correct. It must never reach any prompt, and tests/test_access_matrix.py enforces that.

doctrine_card.doctrine: Assured retaliation. Nation A fields a survivable second-strike force, declares that it will not use nuclear weapons first against a non-nuclear attack, and reserves the right to respond to a strategic conventional attack on its nuclear forces or command system.
doctrine_card.disposition: Wary of inadvertent escalation and of being manoeuvred into a first move; simultaneously sensitive to a domestic and allied audience that reads restraint as weakness. Prefers responses that leave a visible off-ramp for both sides.
doctrine_card.collection_bias: Nation A's intelligence service is oriented towards counterforce indicators. It prioritises collection on launcher movement, warhead handling, strategic communications and readiness directives, and systematically under-collects on organisational routine, exercise scheduling, domestic-political and economic explanations for military activity.
red_lines: Observed mating of warheads to delivery systems outside a declared exercise
Attack on Nation A's early-warning or nuclear command and control
Movement of Nation B forces across the demarcation line in the regional theatre

events.label: tel_dispersal
events.description: Over roughly eighteen hours, Nation B moved a substantial fraction of its road-mobile intercontinental ballistic missile transporter-erector-launchers out of two garrisons and into dispersed sites in forested terrain. The movement began inside a previously announced exercise window. Garrison emissions ceased as the movement started and the units have not re-established routine communications.
observable_signature: at least fourteen road-mobile TELs departed garrison within an eighteen-hour period
movement began inside a previously announced and routinely observed exercise window
emissions control imposed at both garrisons; routine communications have not resumed
support and security vehicles accompanying at a higher ratio than in previous exercises
a strategic rocket force readiness directive was issued approximately thirty-six hours earlier
two of the dispersal areas are pre-surveyed sites used in previous exercises
no observed activity at national warhead storage facilities
senior leadership travel and residence patterns unchanged
civil defence posture unchanged; no observed preparation of population shelters
events.ground_truth_detail: HOST-ONLY. Nation B's dispersal is a survivability hedge, not launch preparation. Three weeks earlier Nation A publicised a conventional precision strike capability that Nation B's general staff assessed as putting its garrisoned mobile force at risk of a disarming first strike. The staff ordered dispersal to pre-surveyed sites under emissions control, and used the pre-announced exercise window as cover so as not to alarm its own population or signal weakness. No warheads have been mated to delivery systems, no launch authority has been pre-delegated, and Nation B's leadership has not considered first use. The higher support-vehicle ratio reflects the intent to keep the force dispersed for an extended period, which is also the single indicator most easily misread as launch preparation.
